existing_entities_and_migrations_inspect.finding: The current finalsource/be baseline contains no TypeORM entities or migrations. DatabaseModule uses autoLoadEntities=true and synchronize=false.

evidence_and_scope.new_table_or_change_required: Create a new users table and corresponding User TypeORM entity for UC-01 registration persistence.
out_of_scope: user profile fields not required by UC-01
account, bill, goal and transaction relationships
user deletion, retention and cascading behavior
changes to existing tables because none are present in the target baseline

entity_mapping.null_default: NOT NULL; database generated; no default
entity_mapping.source_rationale: The UC UML defines User.id as required Integer and the successful API returns it as a JavaScript number.
BR-REG-01 requires an NFC-normalized, trimmed full name of 4 through 25 Unicode-letter characters with single internal spaces. Backend validation remains authoritative for the Unicode pattern.

entity_mapping.mysql_type: VARCHAR(255) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci
entity_mapping.source_rationale: BR-REG-02 caps normalized email at 255; BR-REG-03 and BR-REG-10 require database-protected normalized-email uniqueness under concurrent registration.

entity_mapping.mysql_type: VARCHAR(255) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci
entity_mapping.source_rationale: UC-01 POST-1 and Basic Flow step 9 require a generated unique username derived from the normalized email prefix.

entity_mapping.mysql_type: CHAR(60) CHARACTER SET ascii COLLATE ascii_bin
entity_mapping.source_rationale: BR-REG-09 requires a bcrypt cost-10 hash before persistence; standard bcrypt encoded hashes are 60 ASCII characters.
UC-01 POST-1 requires totalBalance = 0 for a newly registered User; the project database policy requires fixed-precision DECIMAL(19,4) for money.

relationships_and_ownership.ownership_scope: UC-01 creates the root User record. It defines no child relationship, tenant foreign key, cascade or client-provided owner identifier.
relationships_and_ownership.authorization_boundary: Registration is public. The backend generates the User identity and ignores any unsupported owner or id fields through the global whitelist/forbidNonWhitelisted validation configuration.

credential_fields_and_storage_protection: Persist only users.password_hash after bcrypt hashing with cost 10.
Declare User.passwordHash with TypeORM select=false so ordinary repository reads exclude it by default.
allowlisted_registration_response_fields: signed accessToken generated only after successful persistence
sensitive_data_and_exposure.retention_or_deletion_behavior: Unspecified by UC-01 and therefore out of scope; this migration defines no automatic deletion or cascade.
logging_and_export_restrictions: Do not log or export password, confirmPassword, password_hash or JWT values.
Do not include request bodies or credential values in validation, conflict or internal-error logs.

forward_operations: Create users with the approved columns, explicit names, types, nullability and defaults.
Create uq_users_email on email and uq_users_username on username.
Create the User TypeORM entity with every database name explicit and passwordHash select=false.
rollback_operations: Drop the users table, which also drops its primary key, unique constraints and check constraints.
migration_plan.rollback_data_loss_risk: Rollback is destructive for every User row created after the migration. It must not be run against retained data without an explicit researcher-approved recovery/export plan.
migration_plan.lock_backfill_deployment_considerations: The target baseline has no users table or legacy rows, so no backfill is proposed. CREATE TABLE takes a metadata lock but does not rewrite existing application tables. Deploy the migration before starting backend code that registers users.

assumptions.decision: Use INT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT for users.id.
assumptions.basis: The UC UML states Integer and the API/frontend use a JavaScript number; no larger range is supplied.
assumptions.material_alternative: BIGINT UNSIGNED would increase range but would require an explicit API serialization strategy to avoid JavaScript precision loss.

assumptions.decision: Use VARCHAR(255) for username and protect it with uq_users_username.
assumptions.basis: The UC requires a generated unique username derived from an email whose normalized maximum length is 255, but supplies no username length.
assumptions.material_alternative: A shorter explicit username cap would require a sourced truncation/collision policy that UC-01 does not provide.

assumptions.decision: Use utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci for email and username, require stored email to equal LOWER(TRIM(email)), and enforce unique constraints on stored normalized values.
assumptions.basis: BR-REG-02, BR-REG-03 and BR-REG-10 require lowercase/trim normalization and conflict-safe uniqueness.
assumptions.material_alternative: A binary collation would make uniqueness case-sensitive and would rely more heavily on all writers normalizing correctly.

assumptions.decision: Use CHAR(60) ASCII binary for the bcrypt hash and exclude it from default ORM selection.
assumptions.basis: BR-REG-09 fixes bcrypt hashing at cost 10; bcrypt encoded hashes have a fixed 60-character ASCII form.
assumptions.material_alternative: VARCHAR(60) would allow non-fixed-length values without adding UC-backed behavior.

assumptions.decision: Use DECIMAL(19,4) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0000 for total_balance without a nonnegative check.
assumptions.basis: UC-01 requires the initial value zero and project policy fixes monetary storage at DECIMAL(19,4); the broader domain may permit negative balances and UC-01 supplies no invariant forbidding them.
assumptions.material_alternative: A nonnegative check would invent a cross-use-case balance rule.

assumptions.decision: Do not add created_at, updated_at, soft-delete, retention or cascade columns/behavior.
assumptions.basis: UC-01 does not require lifecycle timestamps or deletion semantics; the smallest schema contains only sourced registration fields.
assumptions.material_alternative: Adding lifecycle columns now would expand schema beyond the frozen UC.

assumptions.decision: The rollback drops users and is accepted as destructive only for an explicitly authorized rollback.
assumptions.basis: A reversible create-table migration necessarily removes the created table on down migration.
assumptions.material_alternative: A non-dropping rollback would not restore the pre-migration schema and would leave an unmanaged table.
